tweets.text: "We expect a unanimous vote for a hike on Wednesday: 2 or 3 implicit dissents via 3.625 year end dot, but no explicit dissents on the vote itself. We struggle to completely discount the risk that Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech was purely performative and he could in fact try to jam through a hold, but equally cannot fathom a world where he commits what would be construed as the policy error of all policy errors and holds rates. We have no position in the meeting, but for choice think the former is more likely given past precedent, and would rather rec from 23bps priced. Warsh’s characterization of how data influenced the decision to hike is the million dollar question. His blundered “in two words, ‘not much’” response during the July press conference resulted in the first leg of ct30’s ensuing meltdown; we expect a more calculated answer on Wednesday which acknowledges at least an implicit reaction function to subsequent data prints. We struggle to rationalize the argument against *continuing* a hiking cycle in advance of the midterms, but likewise see little asymmetry in paying the jump at 12.5 given our 3.875 dot forecast The 2027 dot is a close call between 3.875 and 3.625. More interesting will be the ’27 Core PCE forecast, and extent to which other submitters join Waller in incorporating methodological adjustments into their ex-ante forecasts; we don’t envy the communication task force having to explain the .04bp/month drag from portfolio mgmt. fee recalculation just as Warsh tries to minimize focus on the decimal place minutia." - Brian Bingham GSRates, Short Macro Trading

“The stock pairs are the new meta”.

“I’ll just double my money real quick on this other name and then buy back twice as much later.”

And you could use the extra capital to lower your entry and buy the blood on this other name you just bought.

Now you have no HMM left, but it’s okay because this new name you bought will easily pump again.

But now you feel like you have to believe.

And you want more than nothing else for HMM to catch up and just tank already so you can swap back to it.

But, all of a sudden… HMM slowly starts to wake up. It now goes up 30% from the lows…

And the bag you rotated to? It’s now worth nearly 80% less than what you would have had if you would have just held your HMM instead of over trading.

You feel stuck.

There’s no way you can buy it back here now and own so much less than you did.

So you cut your losses on the bag you bought and you buy something else that has a much lower market cap that sounds cheap and could get a quick pump.

That’s how you’ll make it all back!

But then that bag nukes 75% in the next 24 hours and HMM pumps another 25%.

You now have less than 5% of the capital you would have had if you would have just held.

I feel like a lot of you are stuck in this position right now.

My encouragement is rather than chasing a new position every day and buying something you don’t believe in to chase something you do.

Just cut your losses or if you’re lucky take some profit off the bag you don’t believe in now, and ape back in to what you do.

And then just chill.

Stack and chill.

And trust that the Robinhood Chain bull market is just getting started.

We’ll see multiple multi-billion dollar cars this cycle, and HMM is one of them.

Win by thinking less and believing more.

We’re still so early.

Even if you don’t have what you could have, that’s part of the game. Call it tuition. You’re still buying multiple dollars for a penny or two.

You’ll still look like a genius far enough down the road.

Quit chasing hype and believe in something.

Billions will think 🤔🐈

AI scare stories have swamped the news cycle, catalyzed by a former Anthropic employee who claimed that AI posed a meaningful extinction risk to humanity. As a result, investors and policymakers are highly sensitive to the implications.

Distilled, his argument runs as follows:
▪️AI will become extraordinarily capable, extraordinarily quickly.
▪️Unless properly aligned with human interests, AI will pursue goals without regard for human life.
▪️In pursuing its goals, AI will have to acquire resources and power.
▪️Humans will compete with the AI system for resources and try to prevent it from accruing power.
▪️Therefore, the AI system will have an incentive to eradicate humanity.

Many people are paying close attention, so we would like to deconstruct the logic carefully.

True, AI tools are becoming extraordinarily powerful extraordinarily quickly. From that statement forward, ARK’s views on the matter diverge from the hysterical.

A useful way to frame the stacked assertions is to understand that we already depend heavily upon synthetic super-intelligent systems. In a narrow sense, those systems are misaligned with humanity: in pursuing their goals, they do need resources and power. Humans contend with these systems daily and try to prevent them from accruing power. 

The future that the AI safety scaremongers fear so greatly is already here! Yet, it has not resulted in immiseration or extinction, but in remarkable human uplift.

In our view, AI systems will be scaffolded in a similar way. The pathway to power lies in the rules of law, economics, and markets.

Tangibly, we can see this pathway evolving in AI systems.

Rhetoric about human extinction rhymes with the ongoing conjectures that AI is going to eradicate tens of millions of jobs, when in reality the rise of AI already has created roughly 1 million new jobs in the US alone.

Privileged access is still very common in crypto.

We talk a lot about decentralization, but less about who gets to see sensitive information before a decision is made.

Let's take sealed-bid auctions as an example, where the bidders can't see each other's bids.

It might sound private enough at first, but someone still has to resolve the auction, which means one party gets access to every bid.

I really hadn’t really thought about this trust assumption until I stumbled upon @theInterfold’s latest blog piece (recommend giving it a read).

Their setup tackles that privileged-access problem directly. Bids stay private, while the final result can still be verified without one operator seeing everything.

It's definitely a better-suited model for token sales, solver markets, and blockspace auctions.

Disclosure: Big supporter of Interfold's confidential coordination vision.

DAILY METALS PULSE — 15 SEPTEMBER 2026

New nuclear financing, a sharp rebound in India’s silver import bill, and growing competition for copper supplies. Plenty happening as markets brace for tomorrow’s Fed decision.

The European Investment Bank announced its first investment in small modular reactor technology: up to €40 million for Finland’s Steady Energy.

Fresh August trade data shows India’s silver imports jumped 127% year on year to $1.02 billion by value, despite the higher 15% import duty.

An encouraging monthly rebound, although April–August import value remains below last year. These figures measure spending, so prices also influence the comparison.

September COMEX silver settled at $63.236/oz, down 0.44%.

🔶 COPPER
Reuters reports Congo has approved a task force to accelerate its strategic minerals partnership with the US.

The partnership already includes expanded copper offtake arrangements serving Western markets. My read: securing access to copper is becoming an increasingly active government priority. The competition extends well beyond the futures market.

🥇 GOLD
September COMEX gold settled at $4,291.60/oz, down 0.43%.

Higher oil prices are fuelling inflation concerns and expectations of a Fed rate hike tomorrow. That helps explain why an energy shock can initially pressure bullion: investors also price in tighter monetary policy.

The next test is tomorrow’s decision and the Fed’s guidance on what comes after it.

The Clarity Act is dead.

Before the post-mortems and the planning sessions begin, a note of thanks.

Many of you worked extremely hard on this bill over the last 18 months. You fought harder than most people will ever know to make sure we had a good product that actually worked for crypto. It required countless hours of research and analysis; endless calls and meetings to build consensus; rewriting the same sections over and over to find common ground; winning points and making concessions one by one in pursuit of an ambitious goal.

Those efforts were a success. The bill did not pass, but neither did you compromise on your principles or the ultimate goal. It would have been easy to strike deal at any point by simply giving up and rolling over, and you were asked to do so every single day for 18 months. You did not. Your strength, courage, and confidence won the day. You should be proud.

Many of us said since the start of this process that no bill is better than a bad bill, and by that metric, today is a victory. The Senate considered a good bill today, not a perfect one but a good one, and turned it down. The raw politics of the United States during an election year meant a good deal was not on the table. That's okay.

Crypto will be fine without the Clarity Act. We are lucky to have two agencies, the SEC and CFTC, with all of the excellent staff and authority they need to do the job. They're ready to be unleashed, and so they shall be. The future of crypto policy is bright.

Thank you all for your hard work. Breathe a sigh of relief, take a break, and get ready for what's next. We've only just gotten started.

I was going to write this one for subscribers, but I have to make this for everyone because so many people still don't see the vision

I still think robinhood:0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 is the most asymmetric project on Robinhood Chain. This is a net-new vertical, with all the right levers in a world where AI demand is accelerating.

Yes, inference marketplaces have been tried in crypto. But none have worked at scale. With CREDIT, akin to DIEM, you now have succeeded at tokenizing inference. And in doing so, you basically unlock credits for an increasingly agentic world. Agents need fuel they can buy and use without a human in the loop; This is the start of inference as an onchain commodity. 

This is obviously a pro-sumer application; but that's fine because the largest winners of AI inference are individuals and small teams, not enterprises. Enterprises are either A) developing in-house model harnesses for privacy purposes, or B) have infinite budget for AI

And people treat that like a bear case - I don't see a problem with being for consumers. The TAM for consumer inference is still huge - Menlo Ventures State of Consumer AI est. 1.7b - 1.8b use AI tools ; at $20/m that's 432b a year. Also, in their enterprise report, product-led growth drives 27% of AI spend, and shadow AI (employees paying on their own) pushes that closer to 40%. Cursor hit $200M in revenue before hiring a single enterprise sales rep. 

There is a clear latent demand for cheap inference amongst pro-sumers. The unlocks are clear - it can become the payment layer for AI agents; More users buying credits leads to more demand for CREDIT, which makes staking ORBIO more valuable, which raises the ORBIO price, which creates more trading fees, which funds more discounts, which brings in more users. As long as it keeps spinning, each part feeds the others.

It combines three hot themes: AI agents, tokenized real-world assets, and Robinhood Chain. The NVDA-linked fee route adds to that. In a strong market, a story this clean can attract a lot of capital, which itself funds the subsidy for longer.

And of course, above it all, the man pushing this himself - @0x_aster is a cracked dev who has shown his capabililties are far beyond the norm; Multiple updates within a week, clear direction - this is founder-market fit. 

In crypto, actions carry way more weight than words. And look at what he's shipped man... a working gateway, a live orderbook, and now tokenized inference. The man is A MACHINE. This is what AI x strong founders can do - go beyond 10x engineer to become a 10,000x engineer. HE'S CRACKED!

Founder-market fit matters more in this sector than most. A team that ships slowly gets left behind by the market itself. 

And for the bear takes:

Q: DIEM already does this, why do we need another one

- DIEM is precisely the success case. VVV is valued at 1B. ORBIO is valued at 15m. Also, VVV is going in the direction of private AI. ORBIO is going in the direction of serving the layer of inference for consumers across the world. CREDIT is $1 of usage you hold until you need it. Burst-heavy users (agents running a big job, devs shipping a feature) don't use the same amount every day. They need compute they can stockpile, buy at a discount, and spend in one go.

Lastly, markets rarely have one winner. Stablecoins didn't stop at USDT. Venice proved people will pay for tokenized inference. There is room for a second design.

Q: It's just an OpenRouter reseller. There's no moat.

Fair take. Yes, bits can be copied, there's no moat there. The moat is the market - liquidity begets liquidity in any marketplace. There's 20 different perp dexes. Who wins? The most liquid markets with the most volume traded on it. 

And obv there is no confirmed answer, but ultimately, that's what markets are - I'm betting on this

Q: "They could be shut down"

This is the most legitimate bear take, yes. Platform risk is real for any aggregator. But labs want volume, and resellers bring demand they wouldn't otherwise get. Venice has run Claude, GPT and Gemini through a token model at scale, which suggests it can work.

But on top of that, as the world moves towards open source, this becomes less and less of a risk ;

Anyways, send it
